questions.stem: Like Critical Data Elements, Data Ethics is described as a principle. At which levels must it be managed and followed?
options: Managed at individual level and followed at organisation level
Managed at organisation level and followed at individual level
Managed and followed only by IT
Managed by regulators and followed by nobody in particular
Managed and followed only at department level
questions.explanation: Just like CDE, Data Ethics is a principle that must be managed at organisation level and followed at individual level.

questions.stem: What can happen to a company's image if Data Ethics is not taken care of properly?
options: Nothing; ethics has no reputational effect
It improves because of reduced costs
It can be damaged with the general public
It is affected only within the IT department
It attracts more customers
questions.explanation: Data Ethics is a term which, if not taken care of properly, can damage a company's image with the general public.

questions.stem: Which regulatory framework is associated with the European Union in the discussion of Data Ethics?
options: GDPR
PDPR
PIPEDA
Fair Processing Principles
HIPAA
questions.explanation: The regulatory bodies listed are GDPR (European Union), PDPR (Malaysia), PIPEDA (Canada) and Fair Processing Principles (USA).

questions.stem: Which country is associated with PIPEDA among the Data Ethics regulatory bodies listed?
options: Malaysia
USA
European Union
Canada
Australia
questions.explanation: PIPEDA is listed for Canada; PDPR is Malaysia, GDPR is the European Union and Fair Processing Principles is the USA.

questions.stem: Which of the following is listed as the Data Ethics guidance for Malaysia?
options: GDPR
PIPEDA
Fair Processing Principles
CCPA
PDPR
questions.explanation: PDPR is the guidance listed for Malaysia.

questions.stem: What happens if an organisation does not follow all the measures asked for by data regulatory bodies?
options: It receives a warning only
It can be penalised with heavy amounts as penalties
It loses its BI tool licence
It must rebuild its data warehouse
Nothing, as the guidance is voluntary
questions.explanation: If the organisation does not end up following all the measures asked for by regulatory bodies, it can be penalised with heavy penalties.

questions.stem: Which of the following is NOT one of the points organisations should consider when collecting, processing and storing data ethically?
options: Only necessary data should be collected
Data Quality should be there
Data Security and Privacy should be in place
Data should be kept indefinitely in case it is needed later
There should be someone with full ownership
questions.explanation: Organisations should only store and keep data that is required; keeping data indefinitely contradicts that principle.

questions.stem: Which of the following is one of the ethical considerations listed for organisations handling data?
options: Everyone should be aware of the data set
Data should be collected as widely as possible
Ownership should be shared so nobody is accountable
Data quality checks should be avoided to save cost
Data should be stored without security to ease access
questions.explanation: The listed points include: everyone should be aware of the data set, there should be a requirement for the data, only necessary data should be collected, and there should be someone with full ownership.

questions.stem: Why is Data Ethics described as a confusing term in the data domain?
options: Because it applies only to unstructured data
Because it is defined differently by every BI tool
Because many people are unsure how to ensure everyone follows ethics in their day-to-day interactions with data
Because no regulatory body has ever defined it
Because it is purely a technical matter
questions.explanation: Many people are not sure how to assure that everyone follows ethics in their day-to-day activities while interacting with data.

questions.stem: According to the Data Ethics principles, on what basis does each person's level of ethical handling vary?
options: Their seniority in years
Their programming skills
The size of the dataset
The BI tool they use
Their roles and responsibilities
questions.explanation: There are multiple factors involved, and everyone has his or her own level of ethics to handle based on their roles and responsibilities.
